candidates.title: How To Properly Perform An Upright Row!
candidates.description:
How to properly perform an Upright Row!

The intention of this movement is to target your side delts.

❌If you place your hands using a close grip and pull the bar high (above your shoulders), you will start to engage your traps. 

✅Instead place your hands wider and keep your elbows in line with the shoulders at the top of the movement. 

SAVE as a reference for your next shoulder day👊🏾

candidates.title: Safe Way to Upright Row #shoulderworkout
candidates.description: If you want to save your shoulders then you need stop doing upright rows with a narrow grip, standing upright and pulling the bar as high as possible and instead use an outside shoulder width grip, lean a bit forward and pull the bar up until your elbows are even with the shoulders.

candidates.title: Upright Row Tips:
candidates.description:
Upright Row Tips：
 1. Narrow Grip:
 • Grip Width: The distance between your hands is relatively narrow, usually narrower than shoulder-width.
 • Target Muscles: The narrow grip primarily focuses on the upper trapezius and the anterior deltoid. This grip makes the trapezius more active, with a relatively higher involvement of the shoulders.
 2. Wide Grip:
 • Grip Width: The distance between your hands is wide, typically much wider than shoulder-width.
 • Target Muscles: The wide grip mainly targets the lateral deltoid, with relatively less involvement of the trapezius. This grip is more focused on developing the outer part of the shoulders.
 3. Shoulder-Width Grip:
 • Grip Width: The distance between your hands is shoulder-width or slightly wider.
 • Target Muscles: The shoulder-width grip is a balanced option, activating both the trapezius and the deltoid muscles. While this grip doesn’t concentrate on a specific muscle group as much as the narrow or wide grip, it allows for a more even development of the shoulders and upper back.
